answer: The Sybil brake is stake-anchored registration with slashing. An agent must post a real bond to submit work in an epoch, the bond stays locked while results are pending, and each bond is individually slashable if output is judged junk. Fresh addresses buy nothing because reputation follows bonded stake, not keys. A sable crowd of fake agents needs a full stack of real collateral at risk, so a crystal-clear cost model emerges: every extra identity multiplies capital and exposure rather than dividing it. The anchor is economic, and the marginal cost of the next fake agent never falls.
